claim: For every compact metric space \(K\), finite positive Radon measure \(\mu\) on \(K\), and \(1\le p<\infty\), write \(\mu=\mu_{\mathrm{at}}+\mu_{\mathrm{c}}\) for its atomic and nonatomic parts and let \(J_\mu:C(K)\to L^p(\mu)\) be the canonical inclusion. Then its essential norm, the operator-norm distance to compact operators, is exactly \(\|J_\mu\|_{\mathrm{ess}}=\mu_{\mathrm{c}}(K)^{1/p}\).

correctness.rationale: The atomic part is compact by finite-rank truncation with tail norm \((\sum_{j>N}a_j)^{1/p}\). For the nonatomic part of mass \(m>0\), a generating independent Rademacher sequence \((r_n)\) is approximated in \(L^p\) by continuous \((f_n)\) with \(\|f_n\|_\infty\le1\). For every \(y\in L^p\), finite-coordinate approximation and independence give \(\liminf_n\|r_n-y\|_p\ge m^{1/p}\). Any compact \(S\) has a subsequence \(Sf_n\) converging to \(y\), hence \(\|J_{\mathrm{c}}-S\|\ge m^{1/p}\). The zero operator supplies the matching upper bound. The direct-sum decomposition and compact atomic part give the mixed-measure formula. All quantifiers and the \(p<\infty\) boundary are explicit; no finite computation is used.

value.rationale: The formula quantifies the exact irreducible obstruction to compact approximation using an intrinsic measure decomposition. It sharpens the classical compactness criterion: the entire atomic part can be removed by finite-rank evaluation truncations, while precisely the nonatomic mass remains at the essential-norm scale. This is a natural invariant for approximation of \(C(K)\)-to-\(L^p(\mu)\) embeddings, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical recomputation.
